name: Arcane Heist
oracle_text:
You may cast target instant or sorcery card from an opponent's graveyard without paying its mana cost. If that spell would be put into their graveyard, exile it instead.
Cipher (Then you may exile this spell card encoded on a creature you control. Whenever that creature deals combat damage to a player, its controller may cast a copy of the encoded card without paying its mana cost.)
blocked_sentences: You may cast target instant or sorcery card from an opponent's graveyard without paying its mana cost. If that spell would be put into their graveyard, exile it instead.

needs.what: a verification-harness allowance: gate 4's spell-zone check (verify._play_once, and its twin in tests/cards/test_every_card_works.py) admits exile for a spell whose spell_effects declare `encode`, the way a declared exiles_itself / rebound / suspends_itself flag does, because cipher's encoding is a rider on the destination that sends the resolved card to exile (702.99a)
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The DSL already says the whole card: a card_in_graveyard target (any_types Instant/Sorcery, controller opponent), cast_from_hand with objects {target: t1} and exiles: true, and cipher as encode (optional, count 1) plus an exile-zone deals_combat_damage_to_player trigger filtered on encoded_by self running cast_copy. build_sandbox now puts a targetless instant or sorcery in player 1's graveyard for it (graveyard_spell_props), so the card is cast; but the gate's auto-answer encodes it on a creature, the card correctly ends in exile, and gate 4 rejects it with 'arcane_heist is a spell but ended in exile' because the spell-zone allowance widens only for a declared flag and encode is not one. No shipped card uses encode, so every cipher spell fails the same way. Dropping cipher would describe a different card.
